title: Soboro Donburi
subtitle: Japanese minced chicken and scrambled egg rice bowl
excerpt: Soboro donburi is a colourful two-tone rice bowl of finely crumbled sweet-soy chicken and soft scrambled egg served side by side. Each element is cooked separately to keep the flavours clean and the presentation striking.
sourceNotes: Soboro donburi is a popular Japanese bento and home-cooked rice bowl. Soboro refers to the loose, crumbled texture of the meat, achieved by constant stirring over moderate heat. It is eaten across Japan as a quick school-day lunch.

content.text: For the chicken soboro, use a fork or several chopsticks to stir constantly. The goal is a fine, dry crumble with no large pieces. For the egg, gentle heat and slow stirring give the softest result.

items.prepNote: very finely minced or blended in a food processor
beaten with a pinch of salt and 1 tsp mirin

content.text: Cook the rice and keep warm.

Place the chicken, soy sauce, mirin, sake and ginger in a cold frying pan. Set over a medium heat and stir constantly with several chopsticks or a fork until the chicken is cooked through and resembles fine crumbles, about 8 minutes.

Meanwhile heat a small pan over a low heat. Add the beaten eggs and stir slowly with a spatula until they form soft, small curds but are still just moist. Remove from the heat while they still look slightly underdone.
Divide the rice between bowls. Spoon the chicken soboro over one half of each bowl and the scrambled egg over the other half.
Scatter spring onion down the centre and serve immediately.

items.symptom: Chicken is in large chunks rather than fine crumbles.
items.cause: It was not stirred constantly or heat was too high.
items.fix: Stir constantly on medium heat from the very start.

items.symptom: Scrambled eggs are dry and rubbery.
items.cause: They were left on the heat too long.
items.fix: Take the pan off heat while eggs still look slightly wet.
